q: Run on an input, a Turing machine can…
options: halt in two states at once
explain: Exactly one of accept, reject or loop happens. A deterministic TM is only ever in one state.

options: L(M) = L and M halts on every input
L(M) = L, even if M loops on some strings outside L
M halts on every string in L
explain: A decider always halts, with a definite yes or no. A recogniser only has to accept the strings in L.
True. A decider is a recogniser that also happens to halt on everything. The converse is false (topic 24).

options: Exactly the strings that M accepts
The strings on which M halts
The strings on which M loops
explain: Rejected strings and looping strings are both outside L(M).

options: every effectively computable function can be computed by a Turing machine
Turing machines are faster than real computers
explain: It identifies the informal idea of 'algorithm' with Turing-machine computability.

q: Why is the Church–Turing statement called a thesis rather than a theorem?
options: 'Effective procedure' is an informal notion, so it cannot be formally proved
It only applies to finite automata
explain: You cannot prove a formal statement about an informal concept. The thesis is supported by every reasonable model of computation turning out to be equivalent.

q: M₁ recognises L₁ and M₂ recognises L₂. How should a TM recognise L₁ ∪ L₂?
options: Alternate steps of M₁ and M₂ on w, and accept if either accepts
Run M₁ to completion, then run M₂
explain: If M₁ loops on w ∈ L₂, running it first would never let M₂ start. Dovetailing (interleaving the steps) avoids that.

q: The palindrome TM erases one symbol at each end per round. Why does it always halt?
options: Each round makes the remaining input shorter, so the rounds must end
explain: Every round removes two symbols, or stops early. With finitely many symbols, there are finitely many rounds, so the machine is a decider.

q: If a TM M does not accept w, then M rejects w.
explain: False. M might loop forever on w. 'Not accepting' covers both rejecting and looping.

q: Which language can a TM decide but no PDA can recognise?
explain: {ww} is not context-free, but a TM can find the middle and compare the two halves. The others are context-free.
